notes: Saved-account entry and explicit server selection are present. Hosted choices conditionally hide the custom URL; the server remains visible. No clipping observed.

Account and server are grouped, the unverified success mark is removed, and the password has a reveal action. Required-password-change and enterprise provisioning stay explicitly related source states rather than a claim of visible execution.
Restored self-hosted address and US/EU choices. The two-column form keeps every field and action visible; verification-required and uncertain-result branches now have separate scenes.
The code form accepts exactly six digits after whitespace normalization, explains Remember this device, and routes to a method chooser. Submission cannot authenticate in the preview.
The recovery consequence now explicitly covers all configured methods, the code is masked with reveal, and Other methods preserves the verification context.
Switch account is explicit and the hardcoded inactivity reason is removed. PIN has a separate scene; enterprise and Windows Hello availability remains conditional.

The five-word hyphenated fingerprint matches the source and Devices proposal. Cancel is secondary and there is a clear alternate sign-in route. SSO and trust variants remain distinct conditional source references.

Removed the unsupported credential-validity assertion and fabricated countdown. Neutral retry feedback preserves account identity without claiming success. Quarantine and local reset remain explicitly separate source-family references.

All privacy controls and descriptions fit in the 1280x900 frame. PIN setup is reviewable, Windows Hello absence is explained, and emergency-contact wording does not imply all invitations are confirmed.

Website-icon privacy, tray lock behavior, and portable-only browser integration are explicit. About diagnostics are preserved in a disclosure. The MSIX-disabled counterpart is in the managed-policy scene.
Profile edit now has a dedicated prefilled dialog. Generic actions are more descriptive and emergency access has one primary settings home.
Account/server binding, reveal actions, hint guidance and the immediate sign-out consequence are visible. The form validates confirmation before any preview submit.
Current PBKDF2 algorithm, source-supported write bounds and the unlock-speed tradeoff are explicit. No unsupported Argon2 conversion is introduced.
Method states are visible, disable and recovery actions are present, and the redundant Done/Close pair is replaced by a single Close. Setup and recovery routes reveal an identity-verification gate.

The manual setup step is distinguished from reauthentication and completion. The raw setup URI is in an advanced disclosure. The already-enabled/recovery-unavailable source branch remains a conditional family reference.
Named removal has a separate confirmation. Account verification precedes key registration in the proposal text; native verification and unsupported-provider branches remain documented boundaries.

The complete password-based three-step path is now reviewable. Ownership is described as a server-dependent warning rather than a contradictory hard block. OTP and hard-preflight variants remain explicitly conditional.
The message is conditional on registration eligibility, preserves account/server context, and directs users through the email/Web Vault continuation before sign-in.
The uncertain result is distinct from successful registration and recommends sign-in before any new registration attempt.
Final refreshed composition inspected: ordinary methods precede recovery; forward navigation and inline email disclosure use distinct arrows. No clipping observed.
The saved account identity, masked PIN and master-password fallback are visible. This is a separate PIN-configured scenario, not an assertion that every account supports PIN.
Final refreshed composition inspected: Trust this device describes enterprise-SSO decryption and matches the source setting; policy restrictions and MSIX limitations remain explicit.
Only the display name is editable and it is prefilled. Email/server are retained as read-only identity context; the maximum length is visible.
The source minimum of six characters and supported letter/number input are stated. PIN and confirmation are masked and can be inspected with reveal actions.
Only enabled methods are selectable, identity verification is required, and the consequence of removing the last method is clearly stated.
A separate completed state presents an unmistakably synthetic recovery code and explains the consequences of using it. The preview never reaches this state by claiming real activation.
The key, account and server are named. Removal is distinct from deleting vault items and has a destructive final action with a safe Cancel focus.
The middle step requires the exact account email and retains the server. The action advances only to verification, not to deletion.
The final irreversible action binds the account/server and requests the current master password. The preview never dispatches account deletion or fabricates its outcome.
